learningGoals: Understand that 'a' and 'an' are used to talk about a single person, place, animal, or thing. ☝️
Recognize the five vowel heroes (A, E, I, O, U) and their sounds. 🦸‍♂️🦸‍♀️
Learn to confidently use 'an' before words that start with a vowel sound, like 'an apple' or 'an egg'. 🍏
Learn to confidently use 'a' before words that start with a consonant sound, like 'a ball' or 'a cat'. ⚽
keyVocabulary: Vowels - The letters A, E, I, O, U ✨
Consonants - All the other letters in the alphabet like B, C, D, F 🔤
Sound - How a letter is spoken out loud 🗣️
teachingTips: Vowel Hand: Trace your child's hand on a piece of paper and write A, E, I, O, U on the five fingers. Stick it on the fridge to help them remember their vowel heroes! ✋
The Sound Game: Emphasize that it is about the SOUND. Say words aloud slowly, like 'aaah-pple' or 'b-b-ball', so they hear the starting sound clearly before choosing 'A' or 'An'. 👂
House Tour: Walk around the house and point to everyday objects. Playfully ask, 'Is it a table or an table?' Let them correct your silly mistakes! 🏠
Reading Buddy: While reading bedtime stories, pause at the words 'a' or 'an' and ask your child why that specific word was used. It makes reading a fun puzzle! 📚

funActivities.title: A or An Toy Sort 🧸
funActivities.description: Gather a mix of toys (e.g., a car, a ball, an elephant toy, an orange block). Make two boxes or circles on the floor labelled 'A' and 'An'. Have your child pick up a toy, say its name, and place it in the correct spot! 📦

funActivities.title: Vowel Hero High-Five 🙏
funActivities.description: Every time you say a word starting with a vowel sound (like egg, ice cream, ant), your child has to shout 'AN!' and give you a high-five. If it starts with a consonant, they say 'A' and clap once. 👏

funActivities.title: Silly Sentences 🤪
funActivities.description: Make up silly sentences together and let your child fill in the blanks. For example, 'I saw ___ elephant eating ___ banana.' Kids love imagining the funny pictures while practicing their new grammar rules! 🍌
